description: By the door of the Fellowship hall hangs Mother Ash's slate: every vent in the Lowvents that hisses, in the order it began. Mended vents are rubbed out with a thumb. The slate is never shorter in the morning than it was the night before. Under it, on the bench, lie sheet brass, a riveting hammer and a box of rivets that the Fellowship counts every evening, out loud.

options.label: Take the vent at the top of the slate, the one that has been there longest.

success.text: It has been there longest because it is in a cupboard under a stair, behind a family's coal. You patch it on your knees by lamplight and come out with soot to the elbow. Mother Ash rubs the top line off the slate with her thumb and does not look at you while she does it, which is how you know.

failure.text: The seam has rotted further than the slate let on, and the patch tears out with the first rivet, taking a jet of steam across your forearm. The family whose cupboard it is fetch a bowl of cold water without being asked. They have done it before. The vent stays on the slate, at the top.

options.label: Leave twenty Brass Ingots on the bench for the Fellowship to make into vent sleeves.

success.text: The Stoker counting rivets stops counting, counts your ingots instead, and writes a figure on the back of the slate where Mother Ash will see it. Nobody says thank you. Nobody in the Lowvents ever does. Next time you come down the stair, a Stoker you do not know stands aside for you on the landing.
